preamble: Insertion of a rhotic to break vowel hiatus at word or morpheme boundaries. Central Bavarian German has a sandhi rule in which r (or n) is inserted between two vowels across a boundary, even where neither word had an etymological r. Intrusive [ɹ] in non-rhotic English is filed under ∅ > ɹ.

examples.note: r inserted between two vowels across a morpheme boundary as a hiatus breaker
Final n of gegen is lost in the dialect; r, not the etymological n, fills the hiatus

languageExamples.context: Between vowels across a word or morpheme boundary
